newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Caymans Stock Exchange on track - government.
newsitem.headline: Caymans Stock Exchange on track - government.

text.p: The Cayman Islands Stock Exchange, which opened on January 2, is developing as planned and a number of prospective listings have already emerged, said Deborah Drummond, head of the government's Finance and Economic Development Department.
The exchange, known as CSX, "is going forward according to plan," Drummond told Reuters in an interview late Thursday.

She dismissed media accounts that the CSX had no prospects for listings. Ten listing agents were approved in February and they were identifying prospective listings. It was up to them, not the exchange, to bring listings onto the exchange.

"We expect that the listing agents will bring listings prospects to maturity in due course and the exchange will assist in any way possible," she said, adding that there was keen international interest.
"The exchange is viewed as a long-term investment in the financial services sector and our ambitions are geared accordingly."

The CSX specialises in mutual funds and "special purpose" vehicles. The listing rules also provide for international debt securities, debt and equity of domestic companies and secondary listings. Listings such as common stock and Eurobonds could be added in the future, she said.
No date for trading to begin has been announced, but it should be in the very near future, sources close to the CSX said.
The newly appointed CSX chief executive officer, Ann Nealon, formerly policy director at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, is expected to take up her duties in June.
